        How to read these signals

        Two independent GDELT searches. Counts are unique headline URLs returned, up to 40 per stream, not verified events, deaths, aid delivered, or severity. Country names are matched in headline text and plotted at country level, not at event locations. Categories can overlap. A headline mentioning genocide is not a legal determination. ACLED and UCDP links below are references, not active inputs to this pulse.

        Headlines and first-seen times come from GDELT. A match can be incomplete, duplicated or wrong. No matches does not prove that nothing happened. No full articles or private data are copied here.

        Prayer, evidence & understanding

        Four layers. Different kinds of evidence.

        Annual research describes country conditions. Reporting helps you explore recent developments. XRPL confirms public records, not their truth or the location of a person. No map marker means no qualifying public group—not no prayers.

        Interface and guide translations are provided for convenience. Original research, detailed protocols, security instructions and news titles remain in their source language. Review the original before signing.

        Never share exact locations, escape routes, wallet secrets or identifying details about vulnerable people. Prayer focus is not a participant location. Private Capsule contents stay outside this map.

        Currency reference · no payment

        Convert a reference XRP amount into your display currency. This is not a fee quote, a donation request or a value assigned to prayer. Changing the currency cannot change a transaction.

        Use a decimal point, without grouping separators. No amount is sent to the data providers.

        —

        Rates load only when this panel is opened or refreshed. Coinbase supplies an XRP/USD reference; Frankfurter supplies dated ECB foreign-exchange references. Providers receive ordinary network requests, not your wallet, message or entered amount.

        Daily FX references are not executable prices. Missing or old rates stay unavailable. Countries, counts and pressure scores are never converted into money.

        What this map can establish

        The country layer summarizes published research about pressure and violence affecting Christians. The ledger layer proves that qualifying prayer records exist on XRPL. These are different measurements and remain visually separate.

        A change occurring after prayer activity is a descriptive association—not proof that prayer caused the change. Reporting access, conflict, policy, migration, media attention, and many other factors can change the measurements. The dignity of every person comes before the data: these measures do not rank holiness, spiritual worth, or divine favor. They invite careful, compassionate attention—not a verdict on any people.

        Map key

        • ◆Red diamond & ripple: a newly returned violence or persecution report mentions this country. Select to read it.
        • Green circle & ripple: a newly returned report mentions relief, peace or restored freedom. It is a report, not proof of an outcome.
        • Red annual point: higher measured pressure than 2025.
        • Green annual point: lower measured pressure than 2025; not a claim of safety.
        • Gold annual point: no score change. Ring size reflects the 2026 score.
        • Not ranked: not a zero or a claim of safety
        • Solid gold: USCIRF recommended CPC
        • Dashed gold: USCIRF recommended Special Watch List
        • Amber diamond: automated seven-day media-location signal
        • Prayer light: threshold-qualified, validated XRPL prayer aggregate
        • Colored curve: thresholded aggregate support relationship; never a travel, escape, extraction or transaction route

            Private Capsule · local encrypted communication

            Create an encrypted message in this browser, send the ciphertext package through a channel you trust, and give the recovery key separately. The optional NFT is a neutral fingerprint receipt only; it is never a map marker.

            Local-only by default
            High-risk safety boundary: do not enter escape routes, safe-house addresses, current GPS/location, identity documents, passwords, seed phrases, private keys, names of vulnerable third parties or operational movement plans. If a public wallet link could put someone at risk, do not mint the optional receipt—use local encryption only.
            The plaintext is encrypted locally. Message length is padded into 512-byte buckets before encryption to reduce exact-length leakage.

            Local decrypter

            Paste the ciphertext transport JSON and the separate key card. Decryption happens locally; neither value is submitted to JCS, XRPL or the map.

            Persecution research & prayer context

            Country conditions and prayer guidance should come from the current source dossier, not from a map score alone.

            Open Doors country dossiers
            Location and privacy rules
            • Existing NFT and registry records without a structured focus remain visible in totals as “map focus not published.”
            • Public markers never infer a person’s location from a wallet, transaction route, validator, name or prayer. A temporary private prayer light may use the country suggestion made on Sign the Ledger; it remains in this browser and is excluded from exports.
            • JCS V6 records may contain one voluntary prayer-focus or support-focus country/region in signed public memos. It describes what the record concerns, not where the signer is.
            • Broad regions require at least 5 distinct signing accounts; countries require 10, and extreme-pressure countries require 20. Connections require qualifying source and destination groups, distinct parent prayers, and distinct responders.
            • Published area and connection totals are rounded down to five-record bands so a live refresh does not identify a single new contribution.
            • Support curves are descriptive aggregate relationships only. They must never be interpreted as travel paths, extraction routes, safe corridors, movement plans, or transaction routing.
            • These thresholds reduce casual exposure but cannot make public ledger activity anonymous. The map never uses a mileage-radius or synthetic personal coordinate.
            • Public circles require the applicable distinct-account threshold. Wallets, transaction hashes, NFT owners, exact times, and prayer text are never shown on this map.
            • The connected verification form asks for the prayer’s broad focus—not a vulnerable person’s physical location.
            How the XRPL reader works
            • Scans validated account_tx history for the JCS collector rPU6…RyYKd.
            • Accepts JCS V1–V6 public post registry payments and parses only allowlisted memo fields.
            • Resolves V6 community replies to parent prayer records, then releases only aggregate links that satisfy both endpoint and diversity thresholds.
            • Recognizes the current prayer NFT taxon 1246974803 and verifies referenced mint transactions when live transport permits.
            • Uses four public WebSocket endpoints in sequence, then the existing read-only Render proxy as a fallback.
            • Replaces the embedded audited snapshot only if the immutable ledger totals do not regress.
            Evidence limits
            • WWL is Christian-specific advocacy research. Scores measure pressure in five life spheres plus violence; compare scores, not rank movement alone.
            • USCIRF recommendations cover freedom of religion or belief for all faiths and are not a Christian-persecution score.
            • GDELT is automated multilingual media analysis. Its locations are places mentioned near the fixed query, not verified incident locations. Translation, geocoding, duplicates, media access, and false positives affect results.
            • “No comparable data,” “zero records,” “cached,” and “unavailable” are intentionally different states.
            Machine-readable map contract

            The page publishes jcs-prayer-map-protocol-v2 so Verify, future JCS tools, auditors and AI systems can distinguish prayer registry tags, privacy thresholds, refresh handoffs, map display rules and the separate Private Capsule protocol.
